headline: A NEW WAR FOR AN OLD REPUBLIC
short_desc: President Carlisle Addresses the Nation
long_desc: In a nationally televised address from the newly fortified Washington Mall, President Ualani Carlisle gripped the podium and stared down a nation that smelled faintly of gunpowder and existential dread. 'King George III has made his intentions clear,' she said. 'So have we.' Behind her, the Lincoln Memorial statue gave what witnesses described as an encouraging nod.

headline: HAPPY NEW YEAR: Redcoats Ring in Revolution
short_desc: Nation Celebrates Anyway
long_desc: Despite active cannon fire in three states, Americans rang in the New Year with characteristic determination. Sales of sparklers hit record highs. The King issued a formal complaint that confusing his war with a party was tremendously disrespectful. Valley Forge reported a modest surplus of corn. Morale: complicated.

headline: LOVE IN A TIME OF MUSKETS
short_desc: Valentine's Day Dispatches from the Front
long_desc: Commanders across the eastern theater report a spike in heartfelt letters home. The Royal Navy intercepted seventeen love poems and — in a breach of all protocol — read them aloud on deck. With full ceremony. One officer cried. This fact appears in the official intelligence report. The report was classified. It has been leaked.

headline: INDEPENDENCE DAY: We Did It Once We're Doing It Again
short_desc: July 4th Annual Observance
long_desc: Across liberated territory, citizens gathered in town squares, church yards, cornfields, and at least one functioning Atlantic City blackjack table. President Carlisle delivered remarks: 'The first revolution took eight years. We're faster now. Probably.'

headline: HALLOWS' EVE: Mothman Spotted Over West Virginia
short_desc: President Declines to Confirm or Deny
long_desc: Reports of a large winged figure circling the Appalachian highlands have spooked Redcoat supply lines and delighted everyone else. The Department of Mythological Affairs issued a statement: 'The President is aware of the situation.' The Mothman could not be reached for comment.

headline: NASSAU FALLS: THE PIRATES STAND WITH THE REPUBLIC
short_desc: Calico Jack Offers Alliance
long_desc: The Pirate Republic of Nassau does not bother with formalities. When Continental forces secured the harbor, a figure in a particularly dramatic coat — identified in intelligence reports as Calico Jack, nominal commander of what Nassau calls its navy and everyone else calls a well-organized problem — produced a document. The document said, more or less: same enemy, different methods. The alliance was not exactly official. It was extremely effective. The Royal Navy filed three separate objections. All three were intercepted by Nassau privateers. This was considered a reply.

headline: NYC FALLS TO THE REPUBLIC
short_desc: Stock Market Confused Statue of Liberty Visibly Moved
long_desc: New York City has been liberated. The Stock Market resumed operations immediately, issuing seventeen contradictory reports before noon. BUY: Liberty Bonds. SELL: Crown shipping. HOLD: general uncertainty about whether liberty is a growth sector. The Statue of Liberty wept.

headline: GETTYSBURG SECURED
short_desc: Memorial Staff Very Tired of Explaining This Is the Second Time
long_desc: The Gettysburg Memorial has been secured by Continental forces. Tour guides who had continued operating throughout the occupation welcomed the development. 'Twice,' said head docent Patricia Eubanks. 'This field has been important twice.' She did not elaborate.

headline: KENNETT SQUARE FREE
short_desc: Mushroom Capital of the World Emerges From Darkness (Appropriately)
long_desc: The liberation of Kennett Square was celebrated with the largest fungi-themed victory banquet in recorded human history. Crown forces had commandeered the entire mushroom crop. It has been recovered. It is delicious. Continental supply officers are unsure how to log 'liberated mushrooms' in the official ledger but are doing their best.

headline: BRATTLEBORO LIBERATED
short_desc: Green Mountain Boys Celebrate With Locally Grown Provisions
long_desc: Vermont, true to form, has been quietly doing things its own way throughout the occupation. Brattleboro — which produces what the tile manifest lists as 'cannabis' and the supply ledger lists as 'morale crops' — welcomed Continental forces with characteristic Vermont energy: genuine, slightly unfocused, ultimately very effective.

headline: DC FALLS: Government in Temporary Relocation
short_desc: President Carlisle Very Calm Suspiciously Calm
long_desc: Washington DC has fallen. The White House press secretary is calling it 'a strategic redeployment of symbolic infrastructure.' President Carlisle has relocated to Valley Forge — quote, for the poetry of it. Her staff has noted that the poetry of Valley Forge historically involves significant casualties from exposure. The President is aware of this.

headline: GETTYSBURG TAKEN
short_desc: Memorial Docents Maintaining Composure Army Less So
long_desc: Gettysburg has been lost to Crown forces. The memorial staff have remained on-site and are narrating the occupation with exhausted professionalism. 'Three days,' said head docent Patricia Eubanks. 'Last time it was three days.' She is keeping a log. This too shall pass.

headline: PENNSYLVANIA FULLY LIBERATED
short_desc: Birthplace of America Again Officially
long_desc: The Commonwealth of Pennsylvania has been fully secured. President Carlisle flew to Philadelphia and rang the Liberty Bell. It cracked slightly. 'Tradition,' she said. The Appalachian mineral operations are back online. Corn is abundant. Pennsylvania is, as it has always been, extremely Pennsylvania.

headline: VERMONT LIBERATED
short_desc: Green Mountains Free State Insists They Were Always Kind of Free Honestly
long_desc: Vermont has been fully liberated, which the state is accepting with the particular Vermont energy of someone who was already doing things their own way. Brattleboro's morale crop yield is up 23%. The state's collective response to liberation can be summarized as: 'Cool. Anyone want some apples?'

headline: MOTHMAN APPROACHES
short_desc: A Presence in the Dark
long_desc: Something enormous and winged has landed near Harper's Ferry. It is looking at you with profound urgency. It has been trying to tell people things for decades. Nobody listened. President Carlisle is looking back. She is not running.

headline: MOUNT RUSHMORE AWAKENS
short_desc: All Four Have Arrived and They Are Already Arguing
long_desc: The granite has cracked. Four enormous presidents have arrived in the emergency situation room. Washington is attempting to chair the meeting. Roosevelt keeps interrupting. Jefferson has raised a philosophical objection that everyone is ignoring. Lincoln is watching Ualani. 'She's better at this than any of us were,' he says. Nobody disagrees.

headline: FIELD PROMOTION: [COMMANDER_NAME] DISTINGUISHED IN EARLY OPERATIONS
short_desc: [COMMANDER_NAME] Has Earned the First Step.
long_desc: [COMMANDER_NAME] arrived at [TILE_NAME] without a title worth repeating. They leave this phase of the war with one. The record shows: five engagements, two under circumstances that nobody who wasn't there should have survived, and one decision that will be taught in whatever military academies the Republic eventually builds. President Carlisle does not promote lightly. The citation is brief. The name will be remembered.

headline: CITATION FOR EXCEPTIONAL SERVICE: [COMMANDER_NAME] AT [TILE_NAME]
short_desc: [COMMANDER_NAME] Warranted a Second Look. And a Second Promotion.
long_desc: The formal recognition came with a document, a seal, and a room full of officers who had heard the name before and now understood why. [COMMANDER_NAME]'s service at [TILE_NAME] has moved from notable to undeniable. Three separate unit commanders cited them in field reports. One cited them twice, which is unusual and meaningful. President Carlisle signed the citation personally and added a marginal note that the official record omits but the recipient will not forget.

headline: PRESIDENT CARLISLE DELIVERS PERSONAL THANKS TO [COMMANDER_NAME] AT [TILE_NAME]
short_desc: The President Doesn't Visit Everyone. She Visited Them.
long_desc: [COMMANDER_NAME] did not expect the President to arrive in person. Nobody who gets this visit expects it — it is, by design, not on the official schedule. President Carlisle came to [TILE_NAME] without the briefing staff and without the press detail and with exactly the intention she communicated at the door: to thank a specific person, in a specific place, for what they specifically did. What was said in that room is not in the official record. What is in the official record: [COMMANDER_NAME] returned to duty with a bearing that several junior officers described as 'changed.' One said 'galvanized.' The word the President used, privately, was 'deserved.'

headline: JERSEY DEVIL EMERGES FROM THE PINE BARRENS
short_desc: Something Deeply Unusual Has Endorsed the Revolution
long_desc: A creature — hooves, wings, a screech that rattles teeth — has been conducting what witnesses describe as aggressive reconnaissance along Crown supply lines in New Jersey. The Department of Mythological Affairs filed a report. The report said: confirmed. The Governor of New Jersey was asked to comment. He said only 'yeah.' New Jersey knows. New Jersey has always known.

headline: BIGFOOT SIDES WITH THE REVOLUTION
short_desc: Appalachian Footprint Evidence Officially Classified
long_desc: Enormous footprints have been found in eleven separate Appalachian counties, all leading toward Crown fortifications. Intelligence suggests the creature moves with tactical awareness. Reports of Redcoat units filing noise complaints about nighttime woodland disturbances have been confirmed. The Department of Mythological Affairs notes that Bigfoot has expressed solidarity through action rather than statement, which frankly we respect more than the press conferences we have been doing.

headline: THUNDERBIRD ANSWERS THE CALL
short_desc: Indigenous Skies Reclaim Their Sovereignty
long_desc: The great bird has been seen again. Its wingspan shades hilltops. Its call carries three counties. Several Crown signal fires have been disrupted by what officers recorded as unexplained atmospheric interference — which is the military way of writing a very large bird knocked over our stuff. Indigenous communities across the Northern ranges have acknowledged the sighting without surprise. The Department of Mythological Affairs is catching up.

headline: THE HORSEMAN RIDES AGAIN
short_desc: Sleepy Hollow Reports Extremely On-Brand Development
long_desc: A rider with no head — which is notably inconvenient from a military intelligence standpoint but apparently no impediment to aggressive cavalry engagement — has been conducting raids against Crown couriers in the Hudson Valley. The locals are not alarmed. She comes around every generation, said a woman in Tarrytown handing the field reporter a cup of cider. Doesn't like British people. Classic. The Department of Mythological Affairs is filing this one under R for Refreshingly Familiar.

headline: CHESSIE RISES FROM THE BAY
short_desc: Chesapeake Sea Serpent Has Opinions About the Royal Navy
long_desc: Fishermen along the Chesapeake have been reporting something enormous moving beneath the water since the Crown fleet arrived. Naval officers describe wake disturbances inconsistent with known wildlife and a sound that makes men uncomfortable in a primal way. Chessie — known to locals, disputed by scientists, beloved by everyone with a boat — has apparently had enough. Three Royal Navy frigates have filed for unspecified weather damage. The Department of Mythological Affairs filed a counter-report labeling it: sea serpent, friendly.

headline: THE BELL WITCH MANIFESTS IN TENNESSEE
short_desc: Crown Forces in the Southern Theater Reporting Morale Issues
long_desc: Soldiers stationed in the Tennessee highlands are filing complaints. The complaints describe: voices in empty rooms, unexplained bruising, complete inability to sleep, and food that tastes wrong in a way we cannot explain. The Bell Witch is not the Department's most cooperative asset. She operates independently, the Secretary noted. We have a working relationship based on mutual respect and her willingness to terrify our enemies specifically.

headline: OLD IRONSIDES RETURNS TO SERVICE
short_desc: The USS Constitution Has Opinions About King George
long_desc: Something moved in Boston Harbor. Something that should not be moving. The hull of the USS Constitution — battered, ancient, unsinkable — has been observed taking position without a crew aboard. Royal Navy vessels report a ship with no sailors that nonetheless fires with perfect accuracy and appears immune to cannon. The Department of Mythological Affairs is calling it motivated. Old Ironsides has always been impossible to sink. It is apparently also impossible to retire.

headline: THE GUARDIAN OF VALLEY FORGE STIRS
short_desc: Washington's Winter Ground Remembers
long_desc: The ground at Valley Forge is remembering things. The sentries report footsteps in the snow where there are no feet. The cannon fire sounds different near the old encampment — larger, somehow. Like memory has mass. The Department of Mythological Affairs believes this is Washington's army: not the General, not the man, but the army itself — the frozen and the starved and the ones who stayed. They stayed then. They are staying now.

headline: THE SNALLYGASTER DESCENDS ON MARYLAND
short_desc: Half-Reptile Half-Bird Entity Entirely Against the Crown
long_desc: Farmers in the Maryland foothills have been locking their doors. The Snallygaster — which German immigrants brought stories of, and which the mountains apparently confirmed — has returned. It has destroyed two Crown supply depots and one strategic bridge, which it appeared to resent personally. The Department of Mythological Affairs notes: Aggressive, territorial, extremely effective. Not trainable in the conventional sense. We are communicating through what we believe is mutual anti-Crown sentiment.

headline: PAUL REVERE RIDES AGAIN
short_desc: Midnight Rider Returns for Additional Midnight
long_desc: The horse was heard before the rider was seen. Then both were seen: a figure in colonial dress moving at speeds inconsistent with mortality, shouting something at Redcoat outposts. The outposts are gone now. The message, best the Department could reconstruct, was essentially the same as last time. They are here. Wake up. Several Crown officers filed reports describing extreme panic caused by patriotic specter. The Department of Mythological Affairs has awarded Paul Revere the position of Honorary Speed Asset.

headline: THE LIBERTY BELL RINGS
short_desc: Philadelphia Hears What It Needed to Hear
long_desc: It rang. Nobody touched it. The crack is still there — has always been there, will always be there — and still the sound came. Clear and enormous and somehow carrying to every corner of liberated territory simultaneously. Crown forces in earshot reported what they described as an unwillingness to continue. President Carlisle heard it from Washington. She put down her briefing, walked outside, and stood in the cold for a moment. That, she said finally. That is the point.

headline: THE GREEN MOUNTAIN GHOST RIDES
short_desc: Vermont's Impossible Defender Returns
long_desc: The Green Mountain Boys are long dead. Ethan Allen is long dead. The mountain, apparently, is not done with them. Something rides the ridgelines of Vermont at night that leaves no tracks and crosses no roads and is sighted by exactly as many people as believe in it. The Crown detachments in Vermont have been filing retreat requests without specifying the cause. The Department of Mythological Affairs classified the cause as Vermont. This was considered sufficiently explanatory.

headline: THE SKUNK APE EMERGES FROM FLORIDA
short_desc: Floridian Swamp Cryptid Rejects Crown Authority
long_desc: The Florida wetlands have produced something large, fragrant, and extremely motivated. Crown forces in the southern theater have been retreating from territory they held securely two days ago for reasons they will not fully specify in official documents. Unofficial documents say something in the trees. Locals say oh that is just him. Him has been walking through their swamps for generations. He does not like strangers. Crown forces are strangers. The Department of Mythological Affairs notes this with satisfaction.

headline: THE MINUTEMAN IS READY
short_desc: Lexington Calls Once More
long_desc: They said it took a minute's notice. This one took less. The figure appeared on Lexington Green at dawn — musket ready, coat grey with something that might be dust or might be years — and looked east toward the Crown lines, and then looked back at President Carlisle's representatives, and seemed to be asking a question whose answer was already known. Ready. Always ready. The shot that started this the first time still echoes here. The Department of Mythological Affairs is calling this one home.

headline: LINCOLN'S GHOST APPEARS IN WASHINGTON
short_desc: The President Has an Appointment
long_desc: He has been here since 1865. The building knows. The rooms remember. Lincoln does not haunt Washington the way stories say haunting works — he sits in the hard chairs and reads the difficult briefings and sometimes appears at Ualani Carlisle's office door at two in the morning to say something useful about losing things that matter. The arc of history, he said last Tuesday, looking out at the occupation. Bends toward justice. Pause. This is the bending part. He does not seem worried. This helps.

headline: FORT [TILE_NAME]: STRUCTURAL CONCERNS AND A PAMPHLET PROBLEM
short_desc: [COMMANDER_NAME] Has Gone to the Press. All of the Press.
long_desc: The fort at [TILE_NAME] has been deteriorating since approximately the second year of human civilization, but [COMMANDER_NAME] has taken the matter public in the most colonial way available: pamphlets. Pamphlets describing the state of the powder stores. Pamphlets describing the structural integrity of the eastern parapet. Pamphlets, somehow, describing the exact sequence of procurement failures that led to seventeen barrels of what was supposed to be gunpowder turning out to be sawdust. They are being distributed in taverns from here to Philadelphia. Three have been read aloud in church. President Carlisle's advisors have used a word she did not ask to have explained. The garrison is restless. The commander is defiant. The fort is unquestionably falling apart. Choose your approach — then station an army at [TILE_NAME] to carry it out.

headline: PRESIDENT CARLISLE FIRES [COMMANDER_NAME] IN FRONT OF GOD AND THE GARRISON
short_desc: Commander Removed. Effective Immediately. Effectively Loudly.
long_desc: President Carlisle's arrival at [TILE_NAME] was not quiet. Her army was with her. She walked through the gate, past the crumbling parapet that featured in pamphlet four, and found [COMMANDER_NAME] in the command tent surrounded by what appeared to be additional draft pamphlets. The conversation lasted four minutes. 'You are relieved,' the President said. This is the complete transcript. [COMMANDER_NAME] opened his mouth. The President's army was outside. He closed it. The command tent was vacated. A replacement commander has been identified, briefed, and installed before sunset. Their first act was to burn the remaining pamphlets. The President sent a letter. The letter said: good start.

headline: FORT [TILE_NAME] REPAIR ORDER SIGNED — GRIEVANCES RESOLVED
short_desc: Presidential Visit Yields Infrastructure Agreement and Renewed Morale
long_desc: President Carlisle did not arrive with banners. She arrived quietly, with her army, and asked to speak with [COMMANDER_NAME] privately. What happened in that meeting room is not officially recorded. What is recorded is what happened after: repair orders signed by both parties before midnight. The commander's public statements retracted the following morning. [COMMANDER_NAME] described the conversation as 'remarkably productive' and 'a significant improvement on the pamphlet approach.' The fort's structural repairs began at dawn. Supply shipments confirmed. The garrison's morale has been upgraded from 'exhausted and skeptical' to 'cautiously optimistic.' The commander filed a formal statement of loyalty. He filed it twice, which several aides described as thorough. The President has cleared the remainder of the evening. For strategic purposes.

headline: CLASSIFIED DIPLOMATIC PROCEEDINGS AT [TILE_NAME]
short_desc: Details Unavailable. Several Structural Matters Comprehensively Resolved.
long_desc: What follows is classified under the President's personal authority and will not appear in the Continental Congressional Record. What can be confirmed: the proceedings at [TILE_NAME] were thorough. Comprehensive. Extended across several hours and more than one room. [COMMANDER_NAME], who had spent three months producing pamphlets about executive negligence, spent this evening doing something considerably more constructive with his energy. The President employed every diplomatic tool at her disposal. The commander reported in the morning that he had never experienced a more persuasive argument for federal governance. His exact words: 'The President is extremely convincing in private. The Republic is fortunate.' A formal apology has been submitted to the Continental Congress. A personal note — contents sealed — has been received by the President's office and described as 'patriotic.' The fort is repaired. The garrison is loyal. The pamphlets are ash. The President looks, somehow, better rested than she has been in months.

headline: THE REPUBLIC HAS FALLEN
short_desc: King George III Accepts the Surrender. The Coasts Belong to the Crown.
long_desc: The last American metro fell without ceremony. No rousing speech. No dramatic last stand — just the hollow sound of boots on cobblestones and a flag coming down. King George III, through his colonial secretary, has offered terms: the interior states may organize their own governments under British suzerainty. The eastern seaboard — from Maine to Florida — is henceforth Crown territory. President Ualani Carlisle sits in the White House with a cup of coffee that has gone cold and a situation that has gone considerably colder. The Continental Congress has dissolved. Fifteen new flags fly over fifteen new governments that did not exist last week. The Republic, as constituted, is finished. Washington DC stands alone — the last tile, the last address, the last president of the United States of America.

headline: WASHINGTON STANDS ALONE
short_desc: The Last Tile. The Last President. The Last Chance.
long_desc: The White House is quieter than it has ever been. The flags of fifteen states fly over fifteen new governments. The British fleet patrols the Chesapeake. Technically, historically, this is a loss. Ualani Carlisle walks the National Mall at three in the morning — boots on the same stones that Jefferson walked, that Lincoln walked, that every president who felt the weight of the thing too keenly to carry sitting down had walked before her. She is alone. Washington still stands. That, for now, is enough.

headline: STATE DECLARES INDEPENDENCE: [TILE_NAME] RAISES A NEW FLAG
short_desc: The Last Letter Arrived Before Dawn.
long_desc: The proclamation from [TILE_NAME] arrived before the sun did. The governor's signature is at the bottom. The language is formal, grievance-laden, and entirely correct about most of the facts. The state has declared independence from the Republic of the United States, citing federal neglect, unanswered correspondence, and a government that was not there when it was needed. The militia has taken the courthouse. The Continental flag has been replaced. What was once a state of the Republic is now, on paper and at gunpoint, something else entirely. President Carlisle sets the document down very carefully. She knows this name. She knows this place. The question is whether she can get it back — and whether, when she does, she wants to.

headline: [TILE_NAME] RETURNS TO THE REPUBLIC
short_desc: The State Capitol Has Fallen. The Rebellion Is Over.
long_desc: Continental forces have retaken [TILE_NAME] — the courthouse is secured and the rebel flag has come down. The declaration of independence that seemed so permanent three weeks ago is now a historical document filed under 'problems that were solved.' What remains is the question every reconquest faces: what do you do with the people who governed against you? They were your citizens once. They had reasons. Some of those reasons were even correct. The President has to decide what the Republic stands for before sunset — not in theory but in practice and in the faces of the commanders who are waiting to find out if they have jobs tomorrow.

headline: THE ARMY ATE THE SEED CORN
short_desc: Continental Supply Office Files Report Describing Situation as 'Technically Above Zero'
long_desc: The quarterly food assessment has arrived with unusual candor. Reserves have reached a number the quartermaster described as 'technically above zero, which remains the official threshold for catastrophe.' The seed corn designated for spring planting has been consumed. Entirely. By the army. The spring planting is now subject to philosophical revision. This is an agricultural emergency. The President is aware. The fields at [TILE_NAME] are the closest operational farmland. Station the army there to salvage the harvest before the season closes.

headline: PRESIDENT CARLISLE SAVES THE HARVEST
short_desc: Farmers Report She Was 'Unexpectedly Effective in a Corn Emergency'
long_desc: The President arrived at [TILE_NAME] before the roosters did. She did not explain herself. She assessed the fields, spoke with the senior farmhand in a tone the farmhand later described as 'extremely motivating and slightly terrifying,' and proceeded to personally oversee the emergency harvest with the focused energy of someone who has read every briefing and is not going to let corn defeat the Republic. The harvest is back on track. The army has been fed. The farmhand filed a formal statement of gratitude and requested the President not come back because the workers couldn't concentrate. This has been logged as a successful operation.

headline: CROWN VESSELS SPOTTED IN TERRITORIAL WATERS: DOCK AT [TILE_NAME] AT RISK
short_desc: Royal Navy Calls It 'Routine Navigation.' The Harbor Master Calls It Something Else.
long_desc: Three Crown frigates have been conducting what their signals officer described as 'standard maritime operations' within eyeshot of [TILE_NAME]. The harbor master's report uses different language — specifically, the words 'deliberate,' 'provocative,' and 'they keep sailing past the same dock at the same time every morning like they're measuring it.' The dock at [TILE_NAME] represents a critical supply and naval access point. The Crown knows this. They are also measuring it. Choose a response — then station your army at [TILE_NAME] to execute it.

headline: HARBOR SECURED: CROWN FRIGATE RETREATS FROM [TILE_NAME]
short_desc: Continental Garrison Establishes Presence. Royal Navy Files Strongly-Worded Complaint.
long_desc: The Continental garrison at [TILE_NAME] has made its position clear to the Royal Navy: this harbor is not available for measurement, assessment, or casual intimidation. The lead Crown frigate sent a signal requesting clarification of territorial intent. The garrison commander sent back a cannon salute — which is technically a diplomatic communication format, and nobody in the harbor disagreed with the message. The frigate has retreated to open water. The harbor is operational and supply lines are confirmed.

headline: DOCK FACILITIES AT [TILE_NAME] DESTROYED: ACCESS DENIED TO ALL PARTIES
short_desc: Strategic Denial Operation Comprehensively Denies Everything Including Our Own Access.
long_desc: The dock at [TILE_NAME] has been destroyed. This was intentional. The Crown will not be using it. We will also not be using it, which the supply office has noted with measured frustration in a report labeled 'collateral strategic sacrifice.' The fire was efficient and the Crown frigate that had been watching from the harbor mouth has withdrawn — presumably to locate a different dock to measure. The operation is logged as a tactical success. The quartermaster logs it as 'a situation.'

headline: INTELLIGENCE ALERT: CROWN FORCES HAVE LOCATED THE FORGE AT [TILE_NAME]
short_desc: Crown Agents Observed Sketching Schematics. The Sketches Were Detailed. Too Detailed.
long_desc: Continental intelligence reports that Crown agents have been conducting reconnaissance near the forge at [TILE_NAME] for the past week. The intelligence is considered reliable. The agents were seen sketching what appears to be the forge layout, the approach roads, and the shift schedule of the workers. This is not casual interest. The forge at [TILE_NAME] produces a meaningful portion of Continental weapons output. The Crown knows this. They are planning something. Station your army at [TILE_NAME] and choose how to respond before they act.

headline: FORGE SECURED: CROWN ASSAULT PLAN ABANDONED
short_desc: Continental Garrison Arrives. Crown Intelligence Reports Update to 'Heavily Fortified. Do Not.'
long_desc: The Continental garrison has reached [TILE_NAME] and established a perimeter around the forge with the particular energy of people who know exactly what the Crown was planning and are choosing not to allow it. The lead Crown agent, according to intercept intelligence, filed a revised assessment: 'Position is no longer viable for extraction or destruction. Recommend withdrawal.' The recommendation has been accepted. The forge is operational. Production continues. The sketches are burned.

headline: EMERGENCY EXTRACTION: WEAPONS CACHE SECURED — FORGE TEMPORARILY OUT OF SERVICE
short_desc: The Weapons Made It Out. The Forge Did Not Have Time to Pack.
long_desc: Speed was the priority. The garrison reached [TILE_NAME] and immediately began extraction of the weapons cache before Crown forces could move on the position. The extraction was fast. The forge itself sustained damage in the process — not from enemy action but from the particular violence of moving heavy manufacturing equipment at a pace it was not designed for. The weapons are secured. The forge will need time to recover. The Crown found an empty building and one very confused foreman who had not received the memo.

headline: MAGISTRATE [COMMANDER_NAME] UNDER INVESTIGATION FOR REMARKABLE CONDUCT
short_desc: The Courthouse at [TILE_NAME] Has Been Running a Parallel Economy
long_desc: The Office of Continental Accountability has filed a report on the magistrate at [TILE_NAME]. The report is seventy pages. The summary is two words: comprehensive fraud. The specifics include redirected tax receipts, creative reinterpretation of sentencing guidelines in exchange for what the ledger calls 'administrative appreciation,' and a livestock arrangement that involves seventeen cows that legally belong to the courthouse but are living at the magistrate's home in what the investigating officer described as 'suspicious contentment.' The courthouse is technically functioning. It is functioning for [COMMANDER_NAME]. Station your army at [TILE_NAME] to deal with this — then choose your method.

headline: MAGISTRATE REMOVED IN DISGRACE — [TILE_NAME] COURTHOUSE CLEANED
short_desc: Trial Lasted Four Hours. Verdict Required Three Minutes. The Cows Have Been Returned.
long_desc: The public trial of [COMMANDER_NAME] proceeded with the particular efficiency of cases where the evidence arrives in its own wheelbarrow. The magistrate's defense was creative, occasionally coherent, and ultimately not credible to any of the seven witnesses, four ledgers, and seventeen cows that were present. Sentence has been passed. [COMMANDER_NAME] is removed from office, effective immediately. The courthouse at [TILE_NAME] has been purged of the relevant paperwork, the secondary ledger system, and whatever was happening with the back room that nobody was allowed to enter. The community has been informed. The community had already figured it out.

headline: COURTHOUSE REFORMS UNDERWAY AT [TILE_NAME]
short_desc: Presidential Reform Committee Dismantles the Parallel Economy.
long_desc: The President's reform committee has arrived at [TILE_NAME] and begun the work of institutional repair. The courthouse's secondary ledger system has been dismantled. The administrative protocols that enabled [COMMANDER_NAME]'s operation have been replaced with federal standards and a quarterly audit requirement. The seventeen cows have finally been assigned to their correct legal owner. The community is cautious but the ledgers mean what they say for the first time in years. The moral decay that had settled into [TILE_NAME]'s governance is being addressed methodically. It will take time. It is happening.

headline: ARRANGEMENT REACHED AT [TILE_NAME]: COURTHOUSE CONTINUES OPERATING
short_desc: Details Sealed. Auditors Redirected. The Cows Remain Complicated.
long_desc: [COMMANDER_NAME] has accepted a private arrangement with the President's office. The terms are not public. What is public is that the magistrate has agreed to redirect a portion of the administrative receipts to the Continental treasury, signed a loyalty affirmation that is notably more specific than the standard form, and delivered a formal apology that reads as though it was written by someone who understood the consequences of insufficient sincerity. The courthouse continues operations. [COMMANDER_NAME] continues in post, for now, under conditions they have been clearly informed about. The seventeen cows have been placed in administrative limbo pending final determination of ownership.

headline: CANADIAN BORDER INCIDENT AT [TILE_NAME]: THE LINE IS IN QUESTION
short_desc: The Map Says One Thing. The Territory Says Another. Canada Has Opinions.
long_desc: A delegation from the Canadian colonial administration has filed a formal objection to Continental presence at [TILE_NAME], citing territorial claim documents from 1762 that nobody remembered existed. The Continental cartography office has filed a counter-citation from 1754 that also nobody remembered existed. Both documents appear genuine. Both documents draw the line in different places. There is also a third map, origin unclear, that draws the line somewhere else entirely and appears to have been produced by someone who had strong feelings about the matter but limited access to a compass. The territory at [TILE_NAME] is valuable. Choose your approach.

headline: FEDERAL BOUNDARY MARKER PLANTED AT [TILE_NAME]: CANADA FILES OBJECTION
short_desc: The Marker Is In. The Objection Is On File. The Marker Remains In.
long_desc: The Continental garrison has established a clear federal presence at [TILE_NAME] and planted a boundary marker with the kind of permanence that communicates sovereign intent without requiring further explanation. The Canadian colonial administration has filed a formal diplomatic objection that is thorough, well-cited, and has been received, logged, and placed in the appropriate file. The marker is still there. The territory is established as Continental. The cartography office has updated the map. The previous map has been placed in the 'superseded' archive, where it will remain.

headline: SURVEY COMPLETE AT [TILE_NAME]: THE LAND HAS BEEN MEASURED AND IS OURS
short_desc: Affidavit Attached. Measurements Verified. Canada Has Read the Affidavit.
long_desc: A survey team accompanied the Continental garrison to [TILE_NAME] and spent eight days establishing precise geographic coordinates for every notable feature within the disputed boundary zone. The survey was thorough. The report is comprehensive. The affidavit has been signed by three licensed surveyors and notarized by the Continental Secretary of Records. The territory has been formally and legally documented as Continental. Canada has received a copy of the survey. Their cartography office is reviewing it. This is expected to take some time.

headline: FIELD REPORT: [TILE_NAME] GARRISON REPORTING CRITICAL SUPPLY SHORTFALL
short_desc: Continental Army There Has Fewer Than Fifty Men and Substantially Fewer Than Fifty Meals.
long_desc: The garrison at [TILE_NAME] has filed an emergency supply requisition. The word 'emergency' appears eleven times in the document, which is unusual even by the standards of emergency supply requisitions. The commanding officer notes that current food reserves will sustain operations for approximately four more days before the garrison's combat effectiveness transitions from 'limited' to 'theoretical.' The army is stationed. The army is hungry. The army needs a decision now, not next week.

headline: LEGITIMACY CRISIS: THE REPUBLIC'S CLAIM ON ITSELF IS IN QUESTION
short_desc: Public Confidence in Federal Authority Reaches Level Analysts Describe as 'Are You Sure?'
long_desc: The Continental polling operation — which functions mostly through tavern conversations and the content of pamphlets — has produced a finding that the President's advisors are describing as 'a number.' The number represents current public faith in federal governance and it is, to use the technical term, low. The states are restless. The governors are asking questions. The questions are polite but the politeness has the particular texture of politeness that exists in place of something more direct. The Republic's authority depends on its citizens choosing to recognize it. Right now, that choice is under negotiation.

headline: INTELLIGENCE REPORT: COMMANDER [COMMANDER_NAME] MAY BE IN CONTACT WITH THE CROWN
short_desc: Loyalties at [TILE_NAME] Are No Longer Legible From the Outside
long_desc: The intelligence that arrived this morning uses careful language. It describes 'communications of uncertain provenance' between [COMMANDER_NAME] and parties that the report declines to name but whose identity is implied by the word 'Crown' appearing seventeen times in the adjacent paragraphs. [COMMANDER_NAME] has not confirmed or denied. They have, however, been seen in conversation with a man who subsequently boarded a Royal Navy courier vessel, which is the kind of thing that tends to narrow interpretive options. The President has read the report. There are several possible responses.

headline: [TILE_NAME] FALLS TO THE CROWN: HISTORICAL SITE UNDER OCCUPATION
short_desc: The Memorial Has a New Administrator. This Is Not Acceptable.
long_desc: [TILE_NAME] has fallen to Crown forces. The historical site — which has stood through two sieges, one philosophical argument about its significance, and the ongoing presence of head docent Patricia Eubanks — is now under Crown administration. Crown officers have reportedly placed a guard at the entrance and issued a notice that the site is closed 'pending review of its historical accuracy.' Patricia Eubanks has described this review process using language that does not appear in the official field report. The site must be recovered. The docents cannot hold it indefinitely.

headline: [TILE_NAME] LIBERATED: THE MEMORIAL IS OURS AGAIN
short_desc: The Guard Has Come Down. The Docents Have Returned. Patricia Eubanks Has Filed a Report.
long_desc: [TILE_NAME] has been retaken. Continental forces arrived at dawn and the Crown's guard detail — which had been conducting what the Crown called 'administrative review' and Patricia Eubanks calls 'an affront to institutional memory' — has withdrawn. The flag has come down. The Continental flag has gone up. The head docent was on-site before the garrison had finished clearing the building. Her report on the state of the memorial during occupation is sixty-three pages and contains seventeen footnotes that are themselves longer than most reports. The site is restored. Morale in the territory has improved considerably.

headline: CROWN AMBUSH AVERTED: PRESIDENT CARLISLE HOLDS THE WETLANDS
short_desc: Ualani Was Already There. The Crown Did Not Know That.
long_desc: Crown scouts selected [TILE_NAME] for an ambush with what intelligence reports describe as 'reasonable confidence the area was unoccupied.' This confidence was incorrect. President Carlisle's army was already in position. The scouts learned this in sequence: first the outriders, then the main unit, then the entire Crown element, each arriving at the same conclusion approximately seven minutes after the one before them. The President did not appear to find the encounter surprising. She appeared, witnesses report, to have been waiting for it. The wetlands absorbed the skirmish with the particular neutrality of terrain that has seen worse. The Crown force has withdrawn to file a report that will require significant creative editing.

headline: STATE RECEPTION AT [TILE_NAME]: PRESIDENT CARLISLE ATTENDS IN FULL CAPACITY
short_desc: The Courthouse Has Never Looked This Good.
long_desc: The civic officials of [TILE_NAME] have organized a reception at the courthouse with the particular energy of people who have access to the President and intend to use it. The guest list includes three magistrates, the head of the local chamber of commerce, a representative from the Continental treasury office, and — by what appears to be an administrative scheduling error — the woman who runs the town's most successful bakery, who is not backing down. President Carlisle arrived in full presidential capacity. The courthouse has been cleaned. There are flowers. [COMMANDER_NAME] is attempting to look like this was planned.

headline: PRESIDENT CARLISLE VISITS [TILE_NAME]: PRESIDENTIAL ADDRESS AT THE MEMORIAL
short_desc: The Ground Has History. The President Has Remarks.
long_desc: [TILE_NAME] has been on the presidential itinerary since the Republic's founding — a site that the nation considers important enough to protect twice and apparently to argue about between protections. President Carlisle walked the ground before anyone knew she was there. The early morning light caught the memorial stones in a way the official photographer noted as 'extremely usable.' She stood with [COMMANDER_NAME] for what witnesses describe as a long moment of mutual silence that communicated considerably more than most official statements. When she spoke it was brief, historically accurate, and made three soldiers cry. The address will be distributed across liberated territory.

headline: PRESIDENT CARLISLE VISITS FIELD HOSPITAL AT [TILE_NAME]
short_desc: She Knew Their Names. That Is Not an Expression.
long_desc: The field hospital at [TILE_NAME] was not on the official schedule. President Carlisle arrived between two meetings that were on the official schedule, which her press secretary is describing as 'a logistical interlude' and the soldiers are describing as 'the President walked in at four in the morning and sat down and talked to us for two hours.' She knew their names. This is not a metaphor or an embellishment for the historical record — she had read the casualty reports, she remembered the names, and she used them. [COMMANDER_NAME] reports that the army's morale has changed in a way that does not show up in any metric the Continental Army has developed but that everyone in the tent understood immediately.

headline: PRESIDENT CARLISLE MARCHES THROUGH [TILE_NAME] IN THE DEAD OF WINTER
short_desc: Washington Did It Once. The Precedent Is Established.
long_desc: The winter at [TILE_NAME] has been described by the quartermaster as 'technically survivable, in the sense that we have not stopped surviving it.' The terrain is frozen. The army's boots are insufficient for the terrain and their morale is insufficient for the temperature and both of these things were true before President Carlisle arrived. She arrived at dawn with no announcement, wearing what appeared to be the same coat she wore to the State of the Republic address. She walked the perimeter. She addressed the troops by the fire. Her remarks were not uplifting in the conventional sense — they were true, which the troops have later described as considerably more useful than uplifting. By the time the sun was fully up the army had decided to stay.

headline: PRESIDENT CARLISLE CONDUCTS SURPRISE INSPECTION OF FORGE AT [TILE_NAME]
short_desc: Production Numbers Were Good. The President Made Them Better.
long_desc: The forge at [TILE_NAME] runs on coal, iron, and the particular institutional stubbornness of people who have been doing this for twenty years. President Carlisle's arrival was not announced. She appeared in the facility with [COMMANDER_NAME] at the hour the day shift begins and proceeded to ask the sort of questions that indicate she has read every supply ledger, production manifest, and complaint filed in the past six months. The workers found this alarming and then gradually not alarming at all. She understood what they were building. She understood why it mattered. She stayed through the full shift change. Production output, the forge supervisor filed in a report the following morning, had increased by what he called 'an amount attributable to presidential interest in the process.'

headline: CULPER RING CONTACT AT [TILE_NAME]: INTELLIGENCE ASSET REQUESTS MEETING
short_desc: The Message Arrived With No Signature. She Knew Who Sent It.
long_desc: A contact associated with the Culper Ring — the Continental intelligence network that operates through couriers, civilians, and what the Department of Intelligence calls 'a remarkable willingness of ordinary people to notice things' — has requested a meeting at [TILE_NAME]. The request was delivered via a method the intelligence office describes as 'the usual one' and declines to specify further. The contact has information on Crown activities in the adjacent territory. The asset is aware that [TILE_NAME] borders compromised ground. President Carlisle is in position. This is not a coincidence.

headline: CULPER RING INTELLIGENCE RECEIVED: CROWN PLANS CONFIRMED
short_desc: The Asset Delivered. The Map Is Different Now.
long_desc: The Culper contact's information has been verified against three independent sources and confirmed. Crown operations in the adjacent territory are larger than the initial assessment suggested — and their timeline is shorter. The intelligence map has been updated. The President's strategic options have been updated accordingly. The Culper Ring asset has been extracted to a safe house. Their name is not in this report. Their name is not in any report. That is why they are still alive.

headline: PRESIDENT CARLISLE MEETS WITH [COMMANDER_NAME] AT [TILE_NAME]
short_desc: An Alliance Was Discussed. The Discussion Went Well.
long_desc: [COMMANDER_NAME] requested the meeting. This in itself was significant — the independent governors of the eastern territories do not typically ask for presidential audiences, and certainly not on short notice, and certainly not with the particular tone of the message that arrived, which the President's chief of staff described as 'urgent, respectful, and aware that it is urgent and respectful for a reason.' President Carlisle met with [COMMANDER_NAME] at [TILE_NAME] with her army standing at a professionally measured distance. The conversation was by all accounts candid. The Continental cause needs allies who govern territory. [COMMANDER_NAME] governs territory. The math is not complicated.

headline: PRESIDENT CARLISLE ESTABLISHES FRONTIER PRESENCE AT [TILE_NAME]
short_desc: The Northern Edge of the Republic. She Walked It.
long_desc: [TILE_NAME] sits at the boundary where Continental sovereignty makes a statement and Canadian colonial administration files a diplomatic objection. President Carlisle walked the frontier line with her army in a gesture that was simultaneously ceremonial and tactically meaningful — Crown and Canadian observers have been informed that the territory has a presidential presence, and that the presence arrived with an army, and that the army appears comfortable in the terrain. The proclamation was brief. It cited the Republic's founding documents, the history of the territory, and the particular American tradition of showing up at a frontier and describing it as already yours.

headline: MOTHMAN DEESCALATED: THE RIDGE MEETING HOLDS
short_desc: It Stopped Haunting. It's Still Watching. These Are Different.
long_desc: The Department of Mythological Affairs field team has submitted a three-page report on the situation at Harper's Ferry. Summary paragraph: Mothman has ceased indiscriminate haunting. The creature attended the initial contact with what the lead agent describes as 'profound focused attention' and departed to a ridge position that is technically not haunting anything within a twelve-mile radius. The surveillance continues. The disruption does not. The department is calling this success and is actively choosing not to examine the exact nature of the interaction that produced it.

headline: MOTHMAN FORMALLY ALLIES WITH THE CONTINENTAL REPUBLIC
short_desc: The Agreement Required No Words. The Words Came Anyway.
long_desc: President Carlisle went to Harper's Ferry alone. Her security detail was told to stay and did not listen and was subsequently convinced to stay by a look from both the President and the creature that the senior agent described as 'a rethinking of my entire professional situation.' The meeting on the ridge was not recorded. What is recorded is what followed: Mothman, which had been causing generalized supernatural disruption across the eastern highland corridor, has realigned entirely to Continental interests. The Department of Mythological Affairs has filed the paperwork. The paperwork required a new category.

headline: JERSEY DEVIL CEASES SUPPLY ROUTE DISRUPTIONS — PINE BARRENS ACCORD
short_desc: The Wagons Are Getting Through. The Devil Is Still There. It's Fine.
long_desc: New Jersey's most reliable supernatural problem had been operating with comprehensive indifference to the political sympathies of the wagons it destroyed. The DMA field team, through a combination of persistence and what their report calls 'non-hostile presence in the creature's territory over multiple consecutive nights,' has achieved a working arrangement. The Jersey Devil has agreed — through a process that did not involve written documents and which the lead agent has declined to describe in detail — to restrict operations to Crown-affiliated convoys. The Continental seal on the wagon matters, the agent reports. The seal is working.

headline: JERSEY DEVIL FORMALLY ENDORSES THE CONTINENTAL CAUSE
short_desc: New Jersey's Most Complicated Asset Has Chosen a Side.
long_desc: President Carlisle drove to the Pine Barrens edge after dark without her security detail, which her chief of staff has noted in his personal log as 'the second time this week she's done something I wasn't told about.' She returned several hours later. What she said to the Jersey Devil, and what it communicated back, has not been included in the official record. What IS in the record: Crown supply convoys in New Jersey now experience what their logistics office describes as 'selective and targeted interference' with a consistency that suggests coordination rather than random destruction. No Continental convoy has been disrupted since the meeting.

headline: APPALACHIAN PASSES REOPEN: BIGFOOT ACKNOWLEDGES THE REPUBLIC
short_desc: The Mountain Wasn't His Problem. Now It Isn't Our Problem.
long_desc: The Appalachian highlands had been experiencing what military dispatches diplomatically call 'unexpected personnel deterrence events' — which is how the Continental Army describes soldiers refusing to pass through mountain corridors because something very large is watching them from the ridgeline. The DMA field team established sustained presence in the affected region, approached without weapons, and left provisions at the clearing the creature regarded as a meeting location. Three visits later, Bigfoot crossed the clearing and stood still for forty seconds. The agents report this as 'communication.' The mountain passes are open.

headline: BIGFOOT FORMALLY GUIDES THE CONTINENTAL CAUSE THROUGH THE MOUNTAINS
short_desc: He Doesn't Speak. He Moves. That Is Communication.
long_desc: President Carlisle went to the Appalachian clearing alone and sat down. After twenty minutes, the clearing was no longer empty. She sat with the creature for an hour in silence. Neither party required words. Continental forces since that meeting report that mountain routes previously described as difficult and hostile are now navigated with a confidence their officers attribute to 'a general sense that the terrain is cooperative.' Three scouting units reported arranged rocks and disturbed paths pointing the correct direction that they followed to significant tactical advantage. Bigfoot has not been seen again. The signs have not stopped appearing.

headline: THUNDERBIRD STANDS DOWN: STORM ACTIVITY RETURNS TO PREDICTABLE PATTERNS
short_desc: The Sky Has Calmed. The Bird Is Still Up There.
long_desc: The Thunderbird had been disrupting Continental signal fires, weather patterns, and field communications across the Hudson Valley simultaneously — with no apparent concern for whose operations it was disrupting. The DMA's ceremonial approach, conducted through Indigenous liaisons who had been suggesting this methodology for two weeks before the DMA listened, produced immediate results. The ceremony involved offerings, a specific protocol, and what the lead agent describes as 'a complete revision of my understanding of what is negotiable with extremely large birds.' The Thunderbird circles. It is no longer descending. This is meaningfully different.

headline: THUNDERBIRD FORMALLY ALLIES WITH THE CONTINENTAL REPUBLIC
short_desc: The Sky Has Taken a Side. This Is Historically Unusual.
long_desc: The formal agreement with Thunderbird was reached through the Indigenous liaison network. President Carlisle attended the ceremony without her staff, without her security detail, and without — notably — her shoes, a gesture the lead cultural liaison describes as 'exactly correct in a way that suggests someone has been paying attention.' The ceremony is not described in the official record at the liaison's request. The agreement stands. Thunderbird has since been observed disrupting Crown signal fires along the northern border with precision that the DMA's meteorological analysts attribute to 'deliberate and intentional atmospheric intervention by an entity that understands the operational significance of what it is doing.'

headline: THE HORSEMAN ACCEPTS IDENTIFICATION PROTOCOLS — CONTINENTAL COURIERS SAFE
short_desc: The Head Was Not the Problem. The Targeting Was the Problem.
long_desc: Continental couriers in the Hudson Valley had been experiencing the same disruption as Crown couriers, which was technically impressive but logistically catastrophic. The DMA's approach involved a protocol the lead agent describes as 'we showed him a list and he seemed to understand lists.' The list contained Crown courier identification markers. The Horseman reviewed it. Three Crown couriers that week confirmed that the following week featured significantly higher levels of inexplicable mounting accidents than the previous one. No Continental couriers were involved. The protocol is working.

headline: THE HORSEMAN RIDES FOR THE REPUBLIC — FORMALLY
short_desc: He Was Always Going to Choose a Side. She Just Had to Ask.
long_desc: President Carlisle found the Headless Horseman in the Hudson Valley before midnight on a night when neither was expected to be there. She stood in the road and he stopped. The exchange was brief — her words, his silence, and a single gesture that her aide (who was there despite explicit instructions) describes as 'the kind of nod that means something specific and permanent.' The Horseman has since operated with perfect Crown courier interdiction. Not a single Continental messenger in the Hudson Valley has been impeded. The Crown's courier casualty rate in the corridor has reached what their dispatches call 'an unsustainable operational situation.'

headline: CHESSIE REDIRECTS MARITIME OPERATIONS: CHESAPEAKE FISHING RESTORED
short_desc: The Fishing Boats Are Fine Now. The Crown Frigates Are Less Fine.
long_desc: Chesapeake Bay's resident sea creature had been operating with what marine officers described as 'enthusiasm in excess of operational necessity' — meaning it was disrupting commercial fishing alongside Royal Navy operations with identical conviction. The DMA field team coordinated with Chesapeake Bay fishing communities who had, it emerges, been leaving offerings on a specific sandbar for approximately forty years. The offerings were presented. Chessie surfaced, considered the matter for eleven minutes, and returned to the bay. Commercial fishing resumed the following morning. Crown frigates report increased wake disturbances.

headline: CHESSIE FORMALLY PATROLS FOR THE CONTINENTAL NAVY
short_desc: The Chesapeake Has Chosen. The Bay Knows Whose Side It Is On.
long_desc: President Carlisle stood at the water's edge of the Chesapeake at low tide at the specific sandbar the fishing community identified as meaningful. She waded out in the dark. After thirteen minutes, something very large surfaced nearby. The agreement was brief. Her security detail, watching from shore, observed a 'sustained period of proximity' and the President emerging from the water looking 'focused in a way that suggested something specific had been communicated.' Crown frigates in the Chesapeake since report what the Admiralty describes as 'inexplicable structural damage to hulls at depth.' Continental fishing boats report excellent conditions.

headline: BELL WITCH REDIRECTS HAUNTING OPERATIONS TO CROWN-OCCUPIED TERRITORY
short_desc: The Soldiers in Tennessee Can Sleep Now. The Crown Ones Cannot.
long_desc: The Bell Witch of Tennessee had been an equal-opportunity haunter for the duration of the present conflict — afflicting Continental and Crown soldiers with identical supernatural disruption and zero concern for military allegiance. The DMA's approach involved a spiritual practitioner from the local community who had not been consulted by the department despite being available and having opinions about this for months. The three-hour negotiation produced results. Crown-occupied territory in Tennessee reports a significant increase in unexplained disturbances. Continental territory does not.

headline: THE BELL WITCH FORMALLY COMMITS TO THE CONTINENTAL CAUSE
short_desc: She Didn't Need to Be Convinced. She Needed to Be Asked.
long_desc: President Carlisle asked the spiritual practitioner who had negotiated the earlier arrangement to set up a second meeting — just Carlisle and the intermediary, no DMA personnel. The meeting in the Tennessee highlands lasted ninety minutes. The Bell Witch, the practitioner reports, 'had a great deal to say about how this should have been approached in the first place, and the President listened to all of it without interrupting.' The agreement was reached in the final twenty minutes. Crown-occupied Tennessee now experiences supernatural disruption at a level their garrison commanders describe as 'incompatible with maintained occupancy.' Three Crown units have requested redeployment to locations described as 'anywhere that isn't this.'

headline: OLD IRONSIDES ACCEPTS CONTINENTAL NAVAL COMMAND — BOSTON HARBOR STABLE
short_desc: The Ship Has Docked. It Is Waiting. This Is Not Normal Behavior for a Ship.
long_desc: The USS Constitution's autonomous operations had been creating navigational hazards for Continental and Crown vessels alike — its targeting was based on criteria no one in naval command could identify. Port authority at Boston, following extended attempts to communicate with an unmanned vessel, established a signal protocol using flag codes dated to the ship's original commissioning. The ship responded to flag signals. This is not something ships do. The port authority has chosen to process this pragmatically. Old Ironsides is docked and waiting. Its guns are loaded.

headline: OLD IRONSIDES FORMALLY JOINS THE CONTINENTAL NAVY
short_desc: The Ship Has Its Orders. It Seems to Understand Them.
long_desc: The recommissioning ceremony for Old Ironsides was held at Boston Harbor with full naval honors and what the port authority describes as 'an unusually attentive vessel.' President Carlisle addressed the ship directly — her staff noted this without comment and has continued not commenting — and read the commission aloud. When she finished, the ship's bell rang once. The port authority logged this as 'acknowledgment of commission.' Old Ironsides has since operated as the most effective element of the Continental Navy, engaging Crown vessels with targeting precision that no living crew could match. Nobody is asking follow-up questions.

headline: VALLEY FORGE SPIRITS SETTLE — CARLISLE'S ARMY WELCOMED
short_desc: The Ground Recognized Her. It Takes Time.
long_desc: The garrison at Valley Forge had been reporting what their commanding officer called 'an atmosphere of judgment' — the sense that the ground itself was evaluating whether the present army was worthy of occupying it. The DMA recommended President Carlisle visit personally. She did, unannounced, at four in the morning in November. She walked the encampment in silence. What the Guardian communicated during those hours is not recorded. What is recorded is that when she left at dawn, every soldier in the garrison reported that the atmosphere had changed. The verdict had been reached.

headline: VALLEY FORGE GUARDIAN FORMALLY BLESSES THE CONTINENTAL ARMY
short_desc: The Ground Accepted Her Army. That Is Not a Small Thing.
long_desc: President Carlisle spent a night at the Valley Forge encampment. She woke before dawn and walked the original perimeter of Washington's winter camp — alone, in silence, in November. The Guardian walked with her. Not metaphorically. The DMA's spiritual analyst submitted a report using the phrase 'direct and unambiguous supernatural endorsement' fourteen times. The Continental Army stationed at Valley Forge reports a change in its operational capacity that their commanding officer attributes to 'morale, or something close enough to morale that I am not pursuing the distinction further.' The ground that held Washington's army has accepted Carlisle's.

headline: SNALLYGASTER REDIRECTS — CONTINENTAL SUPPLY ROUTES NOW CLEAR
short_desc: It Was Never Personal. It Was Just Hungry.
long_desc: The Snallygaster's approach to Continental supply depots was, intelligence eventually determined, primarily nutritional rather than ideological — it was eating stored provisions because they were there. The DMA's solution involved establishing a designated feeding station adjacent to supply routes, stocked with provisions marked 'NOT FOR SNALLYGASTER' in Continental standard font. The Snallygaster destroyed the sign immediately and consumed the provisions. This was considered satisfactory. Supply depots since that date have not been disturbed. The feeding station requires restocking every nine days.

headline: SNALLYGASTER FORMALLY GUARDS THE CONTINENTAL SUPPLY NETWORK
short_desc: It Has Stopped Eating Our Supplies. It Has Started Eating Theirs.
long_desc: The arrangement reached its formal stage when President Carlisle visited the feeding station in Maryland and waited. The creature arrived twenty minutes later, ate approximately four hundred pounds of provisions with efficiency, and then sat down near the President, which the field agent present describes as 'not something I had a protocol for.' The conversation — described by Carlisle as 'nonverbal but extremely clear' — produced a working relationship. Continental supply routes in the Maryland corridor now have zero unexplained losses. Crown supply operations in the same corridor report what their dispatches call 'persistent heavy losses from an unknown source.'

headline: PAUL REVERE INTEGRATES WITH CONTINENTAL COMMAND — MIDNIGHT RIDES COORDINATED
short_desc: He Was Always Trying to Help. He Needed a Schedule.
long_desc: Paul Revere's midnight rides were entirely sincere. The problem was coordination: his warnings went to Continental counterintelligence positions as readily as to Crown ones, routes were not mapped to current fortifications, and his schedule bore no relationship to actual Crown movements. The DMA's integration protocol involved what the lead agent describes as 'a very patient map session.' Revere listened, reviewed the updated intelligence, asked one question through his established communication method, and his subsequent rides have aligned precisely with Crown courier movements. No Continental positions have been alarmed.

headline: PAUL REVERE FORMALLY INTEGRATES WITH CONTINENTAL INTELLIGENCE
short_desc: He Has Always Been Ready. Now He Knows Where to Go.
long_desc: The formal integration of Paul Revere was, remarkably, the simplest alliance in DMA operational history. He arrived at the designated location, sat down with the intelligence brief, reviewed it completely, and looked at the lead agent with what the agent describes as 'the specific expression of someone who has been doing this alone for too long and is relieved to have a map.' He left immediately. The following week included three Crown courier interceptions, two supply depot locations identified in advance, and one alarm raised with thirty minutes for the Continental garrison to prepare. Revere has asked for a better map. A better map has been provided.

headline: LIBERTY BELL RINGS ON SCHEDULE — CIVILIAN PANIC CEASES
short_desc: It's Not Ringing at 3 A.M. Anymore. This Is an Improvement.
long_desc: Philadelphia had been experiencing what the city's emergency operations office describes as 'irregular patriotic events' — which is how the city officially logs the Liberty Bell ringing without warning at two and three in the morning, producing civilian evacuations and one canal boat running aground during what the captain described as 'a moment of patriotic confusion.' The DMA conducted what the senior member calls 'a direct and surprisingly productive conversation with a bell.' The Bell listened. It has since rung at dawn. It also rang at 6:47 p.m. on a Tuesday, which the DMA categorizes as within acceptable operational parameters.

headline: THE LIBERTY BELL FORMALLY RINGS FOR THE REPUBLIC
short_desc: It Has Always Been Ringing for the Republic. Now It Knows When to Ring.
long_desc: The Liberty Bell does not negotiate in the conventional sense. What it does is respond. President Carlisle went to Independence Hall and stood with the Bell for an hour without talking points. She stood in silence and thought about what she was asking it to do. The Bell rang once at the beginning and once at the end of the hour. The DMA's spiritual analyst believes this constitutes formal agreement. The Bell has since rung exactly when the President needed it to ring — once during a Continental morale crisis, once at the liberation of a key city, and once on a night when Carlisle was reading casualty reports at four in the morning. That last one was just for her. She is grateful for it.

headline: GREEN MOUNTAIN GHOST IDENTIFIES VERMONT MILITIA AS NON-HOSTILE
short_desc: The Ghost Updated Its Friend/Foe Protocol. This Was Necessary.
long_desc: Vermont's spectral irregular force had been engaging Vermont militia units with the same tactical aggression applied to Crown forces. The Vermont militia had been filing incident reports. The DMA field team consulted with Vermont communities who described the situation as 'the Ghost doesn't know who you are yet.' The introduction was arranged through local channels. The Ghost, having received context, withdrew from two contested positions and was subsequently observed operating exclusively in Crown-adjacent territory. Vermont has updated its incident reports accordingly.

headline: GREEN MOUNTAIN GHOST FORMALLY PROTECTS VERMONT FOR THE REPUBLIC
short_desc: The Mountains Have Always Been His. Now They Are Also Ours.
long_desc: President Carlisle drove to the ridge above Brattleboro and stood at the tree line at dusk. The Ghost arrived — not dramatically, just the particular quality of attention the local communities recognize as presence. They stood together. Carlisle asked one question. The Ghost's response, described by the interpreter she brought, was 'the mountains themselves agreeing.' Crown forces in Vermont have begun what their dispatches call 'strategic repositioning' out of terrain they could not operate in. The terrain has not changed. The Ghost has.

headline: MOUNT RUSHMORE COUNCIL REACHES INTERNAL CONSENSUS — DEBATES FORMALIZED
short_desc: They Have Agreed to Disagree Quietly. This Is Progress.
long_desc: The four stone presidents had been engaged in what the DMA's report describes as 'a continuous and very loud policy discussion that does not account for the acoustic impact on the surrounding region.' Washington attempted to chair. Roosevelt continued interrupting. Jefferson raised structural objections. Lincoln sat quietly and looked troubled. The civilian disruption from four very large men arguing about constitutional theory at unreasonable volume had reached the level of a formal noise ordinance complaint filed with no one in particular. The DMA intervention imposed one agenda item and a strict time limit. The debates are now held in session. The volume has decreased. The topics have not.

headline: THE RUSHMORE COUNCIL FORMALLY ENDORSES PRESIDENT CARLISLE
short_desc: They Came to a Vote. The Vote Was Unanimous. Lincoln Broke the Tie.
long_desc: The four stone presidents convened for a final session on the matter of President Ualani Carlisle's administration. Washington presented the case. Roosevelt called it excellent and interrupted three times. Jefferson raised a procedural objection that was noted, recorded, and overruled. Lincoln, who had been quiet throughout, spoke last. His remarks were brief — the DMA transcript records approximately fourteen words — and produced immediate consensus. The formal endorsement was made in the manner available to entities made of granite: each looked at her for a sustained moment and she looked back. Lincoln's sustained moment was the longest. The endorsement stands.

headline: SKUNK APE WITHDRAWS FROM ACTIVE DISRUPTION ZONES — SOUTHERN OPERATIONS STABLE
short_desc: It Smells Worse Than Before. But It's Staying in the Swamp.
long_desc: The Skunk Ape's excursions from the Florida wetlands into Continental operating territory had been causing what southern field command describes as 'substantial logistical and morale complications.' The DMA's approach relied entirely on local Florida homesteaders who had been coexisting with the creature for generations. Their method involved a specific frequency of sound produced by a specific instrument at a specific distance from the creature's patrol area. The Skunk Ape listened. It returned to the swamp. The frequency and instrument have been added to the field manual as Protocol 7.

headline: SKUNK APE FORMALLY PATROLS FLORIDA FOR THE CONTINENTAL REPUBLIC
short_desc: The Swamp Is His. The Republic Is Grateful.
long_desc: The formal commitment was negotiated entirely through the Florida homesteader network with zero DMA involvement, which the homesteaders view as improvement and the DMA views as a departmental lesson. President Carlisle visited the edge of the Skunk Ape's territory — the boundary where it decides whether strangers are threats. She stood there. The Skunk Ape came to the boundary. They spent forty minutes in proximity, neither advancing, both aware of exactly what was being negotiated. Crown forces in the Florida theater have since begun what their dispatches describe as 'unexpected and persistent difficulty with swamp terrain' they had managed fine in previous months.

headline: THE MINUTEMAN ACKNOWLEDGES CONTINENTAL FORCES — LEXINGTON GREEN ACCESS RESTORED
short_desc: He Wasn't Going to Stand Down for Anyone. He Did Anyway.
long_desc: The eternal Minuteman at Lexington had been challenging every military unit approaching the Green — Continental, Crown, civilian militia — with what witnesses describe as 'extremely focused attention and an expression that suggests the concept of surrender has not entered his operational framework.' Three Continental units had been turned back. The DMA's recommendation was that a senior officer approach on foot alone, without visible weapons, in formal Continental uniform. The officer who performed this approach filed a report consisting primarily of: 'He looked at me for a long time and then stepped aside.' Access to Lexington Green has been restored.

headline: THE MINUTEMAN FORMALLY DECLARES FOR THE CONTINENTAL REPUBLIC
short_desc: He Said One Thing. It Was Enough.
long_desc: The formal declaration came at Lexington Green at dawn. President Carlisle arrived early and stood on the Green and waited. He came at first light from the direction of the old battle position, musket ready, in the posture witnesses describe as 'someone who has never once been unprepared for anything.' She did not speak first. He did. The DMA transcript records three sentences. Two were about the Republic. One was about her specifically. Her aide, present against instructions, describes it as 'the most direct presidential endorsement I have ever heard.' The Minuteman has formally declared the Continental Army as his army and President Carlisle as his President.

headline: LINCOLN'S GHOST ESTABLISHES OFFICE HOURS — PRESIDENTIAL SCHEDULE RESTORED
short_desc: He's Still Here. He Now Knocks.
long_desc: Abraham Lincoln's ghost had been appearing in the White House executive quarters at two and three in the morning regardless of scheduling, affecting President Carlisle's operational capacity in a way the press secretary categorized as 'a situation we are not equipped to communicate publicly.' The DMA's solution was endorsed by the President personally: she sat down with Lincoln for two hours, listened without interruption, and asked two questions. Lincoln, the President told her senior staff, 'had been trying to say something for a long time and needed someone to actually listen.' He now appears at scheduled intervals. He knocks. The President has cleared Thursday evenings.

headline: LINCOLN FORMALLY ENDORSES PRESIDENT CARLISLE'S ADMINISTRATION
short_desc: He Has Been Waiting to Say This Since 1865.
long_desc: The formal endorsement meeting took place on a Thursday evening, as scheduled. Lincoln arrived on time. He sat across from Carlisle at the long table in the executive quarters and told her, for the first time without interruption or qualification, what he had been trying to tell every president who passed through these rooms since his own presidency ended. What he said is in her personal record, not the public record, because it was meant for her. What she has shared: he told her the arc bends toward justice. He said this is the bending. He said she is exactly who the Republic needs for this specific moment. He said he has not been this certain about something since the Emancipation Proclamation.
